question: Does the swift arising of the cognition justify inferring hidden conceptual construction?
premises: The cognition arises so swiftly that it is not clearly noticed.
The opponent infers from this lack of noticing that conceptual construction is present.
The author presents this inference as the opponent's position.
inference: The opponent concludes that the unnoticed swift cognition is itself conceptual construction, but this rests only on its not being noticed.
plain_english: Because this cognition arises very quickly, it is not clearly noticed; so the opponent infers that it must be conceptual construction. That is the move being stated here.
